Class WhoAdminEndpoints

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.who.admin.WhoAdminEndpoints
All Implemented Interfaces:
BrowserEndpoints, StatelessEndpoints
public class WhoAdminEndpoints extends Object implements BrowserEndpoints, StatelessEndpoints
Adds who's admin endpoints under who.base-path: /identities, to list, read, deactivate and reactivate identities and to assign and remove their roles, and /roles, to list the roles that exist. Each needs a permission from WhoAdminPermissions, which any who sign-in may carry: a browser session, a bearer token, or an API key scoped to it. So the endpoints go on every browser chain and every stateless chain: this is both BrowserEndpoints and StatelessEndpoints. A browser session that changes an identity or its roles must have signed in recently; a bearer token or an API key need not. A caller may assign only roles within its own permissions, may change only identities that do not outrank it, and may not leave no active identity able to manage identities.

    • WhoAdminEndpoints

      public WhoAdminEndpoints(WhoPaths paths, IdentityRepository identities, WhoService whoService, RbacService rbac, @Nullable IdentityEmails emails, @Nullable LastCredentialGuard guard, LastAdminGuard lastAdmin, WhoSessionSecurityContextRepository sessions, WhoExceptionHandoff handoff, tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper jsonMapper, Clock clock, Duration recentSignIn)
      Creates the endpoints.
      Parameters:
      paths - where the endpoints live
      identities - pages through and reads identities
      whoService - deactivates and reactivates identities
      rbac - reads roles and assigns and removes them
      emails - the identities' email addresses; null without email sign-in, when the endpoints show no addresses and refuse a search by address
      guard - counts each identity's sign-in credentials; null when there is none, when the counts are empty
      lastAdmin - keeps deactivations and role removals from leaving no one who may manage identities
      sessions - tells a browser session from a bearer token or an API key, and reads its sign-in time
      handoff - answers errors through the application's exception handling
      jsonMapper - reads the request bodies; who writes the answers with its own mapper
      clock - the current time
      recentSignIn - how recently a browser session must have signed in to change an identity
